newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Historians seek wartime witnesses to Swiss role.
newsitem.headline: Historians seek wartime witnesses to Swiss role.

text.p: International historians probing Switzerland's past as a secretive banking centre during World War Two called on Thursday for ageing witnesses to come forward with lost information on the wartime flow of wealth.
The panel of nine historians said it wanted to hear from people such as former bankers, insurance company employees and diplomats.
"In addition, the ICE will welcome any information which may be provided by (former) jewellers, art dealers and hotel staff, etc," the panel said in a statement,

ICE stands for Independent Commission of Experts, the panel set up by the Swiss government to probe accusations that Switzerland profited cynically from Nazi loot and from accounts left by Jews and others murdered in the Holocaust.

The ICE said it wanted statements from people whose jobs or personal records gave them an insight into the trail of assets brought to Switzerland, both by Nazis and by refugees seeking to protect their belongings in safe Swiss vaults.
It also wanted information on Swiss business abroad and on how wartime refugees and prisoners were treated in Switzerland.

The commission said it would take requests and statements in writing under the address: Independent Commission of Experts: Switzerland - Second World War, "Contemporary Witnesses", P.O. Box 362, CH-3000 Berne 6, Switzerland. Fax: 0041-31-325 1238.
The commission said it was also setting up two multilingual telephone lines for witnesses to make contact.

From August 18, calls in English and German would be taken on Thursday and Fridays under the Swiss number 0041-31-325 1241. Calls in Italian would be taken on Tuesdays and in French on Wednesdays under the number 0041-31-325 1239.
The ICE is headed by Swiss professor of business history Jean-Francois Bergier and includes Jewish and non-Jewish historians from the the United States, Israel and Poland.
